Run against supported SQL Server provider and two independent DbContext/process instances; assert database-level invariant.
acceptance_criteria: A documented owner policy establishes the active-day scope (global or per defined partition).

If global single-active-day remains intended, every Open/Reopen transition is serialized or constrained by database-enforced uniqueness so concurrent instances cannot persist more than one active day.
A losing concurrency attempt leaves no partial state and the existing same-request replay contract remains intact.

specifications.title: Call Center labels a cancelled unpaid electronic order as collectible on delivery
specifications.root_cause: The payment display infers collect-on-delivery solely from IsPaid=false after special-casing only pending electronic status; it ignores order cancellation and cancelled electronic status.
specifications.impact: Conflicting operational message can misinform staff/customer or driver about collection due. Visible Cancelled status mitigates. No actual collection/ledger loss proven.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Make payment text state-aware: cancelled orders should show cancelled/no collection, pending transfers stay unconfirmed, settled orders stay paid, and collect-on-delivery is reserved for active unpaid orders that satisfy COD semantics. Confirm the preferred Arabic copy with owner if wording is material.
required_regression_tests: Projection test for cancelled + unpaid + electronic status cancelled: no collect-at-delivery label.
Controls for active COD, pending electronic, and paid orders.
Call Center lookup view-model test asserts status/payment rows do not conflict.
acceptance_criteria: No cancelled order is described as collectible at delivery.
Active COD remains collectible; pending electronic remains unconfirmed; paid remains paid.
No database/financial movement is introduced by the presentation correction.

specifications.title: Unvalidated denomination and unchecked arithmetic can corrupt finalized count values
specifications.root_cause: Arithmetic and domain validation are not bounded at the finalization boundary; persisted audit data records the derived result without enforcing the supported denomination set or representable totals.
specifications.impact: Could finalize and audit a mathematically incorrect cash total/difference. Existing evidence does not show direct treasury posting, shift settlement, or close-blocker override; do not characterize as cash loss.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Owner must first decide whether ExpectedPiastres is a client-supplied comparison target or must be derived from a server-authoritative snapshot. Then whitelist supported positive denominations and bound each quantity/aggregate; use checked multiply, sum, and difference and convert overflow/invalid rows to explicit domain rejection. Preserve agreed negative-quantity compatibility semantics or reject only by explicit policy.
required_regression_tests: Domain tests for every allowed denomination, unsupported/zero/negative denomination, maximum quantity, multiplication overflow, aggregate overflow, and difference overflow.
Authorized handler test proves invalid input creates neither count nor audit record; valid input persists exact values atomically.
Endpoint test verifies invalid input maps to a deliberate client error.
Verify whether finalized cash-count data participates in close reconciliation and that any such use is server-validated.
Build/run arithmetic behavior under the actual net8 deployment configuration.
acceptance_criteria: All accepted values fall within explicit denomination and monetary bounds; no wraparound reaches persisted count/audit.
Rejected values produce no partial count/audit writes.
ExpectedPiastres authority and negative quantity semantics are documented and covered.
Any reconciliation consumer uses the validated result or independently recomputes the expected value.

specifications.title: Close snapshot revision and authoritative-row admission lack an explicit shared invariant
specifications.root_cause: Read/status admission outside transaction plus Count+1/demotion lacks explicit perday uniqueness/state-token enforcement in inspected source.
specifications.impact: Source lacks explicit common day admission lock/state token and schema uniqueness for archival invariants; duplicate-current/same-revision outcome remains a qualified provider-dependent candidate, not reproduced corruption.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Do not implement a concurrency fix based on assumed SQL ordering. First test provider schedule; if admission gap manifests, use common day lock/state predicate plus explicit snapshot uniqueness/authority invariant.
required_regression_tests: Barrier two distinct close IDs around count/demotion in disposable SQL Server; capture EF DML and locks.
Verify authoritative row, revisions and day pointer across both serialization outcomes/history.
acceptance_criteria: Disposable SQL Server controlled schedule establishes actual DML/lock outcome before code fix is chosen.
After any accepted close ordering there is exactly one authoritative snapshot, coherent day pointer, and valid monotone unique revision; losing close leaves no partial mutation.

specifications.title: Attendance corrections revalue old effects at current rates instead of posted monetary basis
specifications.root_cause: Correction reads current employee DailyWage/current Settings then recomputes BOTH old and new overtime/penalty. It never reads frozen actual original amount/rate or cumulative prior correction effect for delta. Row+ledger serialization and immutable retry audit are real controls, but do not restore old monetary basis.
specifications.impact: Potential over/under reconciliation relative to actual posted effect; authoritative correction valuation policy unresolved. No actual employee loss, runtime record, payout or SQL acceptance verified.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: After owner decision, calculate correction delta against actual posted original facts and cumulative linked adjustments, append only; preserve idempotency, locks, and freeze rules. Do not mint historical credits automatically.
required_regression_tests: Original fixed-rate overtime then settings changed then correction; assert owner-approved reversal basis.
Change multiplier/grace/workday, penalty to zero, sequential corrections/return to original hours, replay and frozen/paid period controls.
acceptance_criteria: Owner-approved correction basis is documented; adjustments reconcile original posted facts and prior corrections without accidental over/under reversal.
Same-key retry and interleaved sequential corrections remain atomic, auditable, and consistent with frozen/paid period policy.

specifications.title: Delivery report field labeled expected unsettled custody aggregates collected amount instead
specifications.root_cause: Delivery report field labeled expected unsettled custody aggregates collected amount instead
specifications.impact: If the DTO/UI contract means expected cash at driver risk, the report underreports that exposure while delivery is in transit and diverges from the owner dashboard. If it intentionally means cash already collected but not settled, the aggregation may be deliberate but DTO name and tests are misleading. No loss, duplicate payment, or ledger corruption is established.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Confirm report contract. Existing DTO name, owner dashboard, and test comments support ExpectedPiastres: if that is the intended meaning, sum c.ExpectedPiastres. If the intended metric is collected-but-unsettled, rename the DTO/display and retain/add a distinct expected-at-risk metric so the two values are not conflated.
required_regression_tests: Delivery query test asserting ExpectedUnsettledCustody aggregates unremitted in-flight orders only.
End-of-shift reconciliation test asserting remitted cash is excluded from courier custody balance.
acceptance_criteria: DTO field name and source aggregate express the same amount.
Owner dashboard and delivery report agree for the same non-settled custody cohort when they claim to show expected custody.
In-transit and variance cases are covered by tests; no real printer or financial operation is needed.
Historical statement temporal semantics are documented separately.
Before delivery, delivery report and owner dashboard agree on expected cash responsibility for the same open custody cohort while collected remains zero.

specifications.title: Server accepts a negative product-variant price that can reduce checkout totals while stock is consumed
specifications.root_cause: Server accepts a negative product-variant price that can reduce checkout totals while stock is consumed
specifications.impact: Potential undercharge or zero-payable order with stock consumption; actual financial incidence and owner policy are unverified.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Confirm whether zero-priced variants are allowed. If prices must be positive, centralize the invariant at server command boundaries and checkout resolution, and evaluate a DB check constraint after legacy-row inventory. Preserve signed Money for legitimate ledger deltas.
required_regression_tests: Domain validation test asserting ProductVariant.PricePiastres >= 0 on create/update.
Checkout integration test submitting item with negative price asserting rejection with HTTP 422.
acceptance_criteria: Owner-approved variant price domain is enforced server-side and at checkout.
Invalid variant configuration cannot create underpriced/free stock-consuming checkout.
No financial side effect occurs on rejection.
Valid positive variants and approved prices remain compatible.

specifications.title: Unknown once-per-order packaging cost does not invalidate aggregate profit completeness
specifications.root_cause: Completeness boolean uses dish-line counters while food-cost total also includes separately accumulated order-level packaging; packaging unknown state is not passed to profitability completeness calculation.
specifications.impact: Profitability result can be numerically computed and marked complete although packaging costs are excluded; reports can overstate gross/operating profit. This concerns report completeness, not ledger posting or realized cash loss.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Carry an explicit aggregate cost-coverage/completeness signal across dish and order-packaging components into profitability calculation and DTO, preserving distinct dish counts and per-order packaging cardinality. Keep missing names. Do not convert packaging unknowns into fabricated sold dish-line counts.
required_regression_tests: Known dish plus unknown active packaging returns IsComplete=false and does not present the aggregate profit as fully costed.
Known packaging adds exact configured cost once per order and retains true completeness.
No active packaging rule remains known optional zero.
Multiple dishes in one order versus multiple orders preserves packaging count/cost cardinality.
DTO/API and UI communicate incomplete state consistently alongside missing item names.
acceptance_criteria: IsComplete is false whenever any sold dish or applicable packaging component is unknown.
The amount excludes unknown cost but is visibly and machine-readably partial; counts retain their documented units.
Known/optional-zero cases preserve existing results and packaging charges are applied exactly once per applicable order.

specifications.title: Concurrent opposite prep edges can evade pretransaction cycle admission
specifications.root_cause: Cycle validation is a shared-graph predicate read before the transaction, while each transaction writes only one recipe; no database-level serialization/revalidation of the graph-wide invariant is visible.
specifications.impact: Predicted active prep-recipe cycle can be persisted despite save-time cycle rejection; costing becomes Unknown/incomplete for affected paths and report reliability falls. No direct treasury, inventory movement, or ledger posting from recipe save is evidenced.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Coordinate graph mutations with a transaction-scoped shared graph revision/lock, then revalidate against the current graph before persisting. Alternatively use serializable predicate validation with bounded retry and consistent cross-process semantics. Retain defensive Unknown cycle guard for existing/legacy data.
required_regression_tests: Barrier-controlled opposite-edge concurrent save: at most one can commit; loser receives stable cycle/conflict error.
Two unrelated acyclic concurrent recipe saves both succeed if product policy permits.
Sequential cycle rejection remains.
Legacy cyclic fixture terminates and returns Unknown/incomplete, with report not presenting complete cost.
Exercise recipe replacement and output identity changes under same graph coordination.
acceptance_criteria: The active prep graph remains acyclic after every successful save, including concurrent saves through multiple server processes.
A race loser causes no partial recipe/line replacement.
Unrelated valid edits retain expected concurrency; bounded retry/conflict behavior is documented.
Costing defense remains finite and conservative for pre-existing invalid data.

specifications.title: Overlapping full-refund replay can reject after same-key sibling committed
specifications.root_cause: Durable refund-key lookup happens before parent order serialization, with no repeat lookup after sibling full refund changes refundable state; DomainException cap rejection is not handled by saved-receipt recovery catch.
specifications.impact: Conditional misleading failure for one concurrent duplicate acknowledgement; later sequential same-key retry recovers. No new financial movement, direct moneyloss, overrefund or permanentclientloop established.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Recheck same-key durable refund receipt after acquiring order lock and before cap rejection; preserve actor/order/payload binding, cap and funds rules. Do not broadly treat DomainException as replay.
required_regression_tests: Overlapping full-amount same-key refund: second request begins lookup before first commit, then after lock sees same committed receipt.
Existing partial same-key concurrency control; distinct-key over-cap, mismatch binding and failed-first sibling.
acceptance_criteria: After order lock, exact same-key sibling commit is returned as replay without second refund or misleading cap error.
Distinct-key refund cap and mismatched order/key binding remain enforced; failed sibling does not fabricate success.

specifications.title: Reversed report endpoints normalize sales but independently filter cost with contradictory date bounds
specifications.root_cause: Range ordering handled inconsistently between normalized sales UTC interval and raw cost/date series consumers.
specifications.impact: Misleading cost/profit/report period, not a proven money posting or authorization bypass. Static financial report correctness candidate.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Normalize or reject reversed date endpoints once at shared request boundary and pass one interval to sales, cost, expenses, and date-series calculations.
required_regression_tests: Pure forward/same/reversed date range and Days/DayCount consistency.
Authorized seeded report nonzero sales/known recipe cost reversed endpoints; direct food-cost/expense endpoints use same contract.
acceptance_criteria: Reversed endpoints either normalize once for every report series or are rejected consistently; sales, food cost, expenses, days and day count use same interval.
Forward, same-day, reversed, and boundary-date reports agree across DTO and direct endpoints.

specifications.title: SafeDrop may attribute a later drawer movement to a closed shift and change its reprinted breakdown
specifications.root_cause: SafeDrop validates only that the request ShiftId exists; it does not require the referenced shift to remain Open. It posts with the current open BusinessDayId plus that request ShiftId. ShiftReconciliation later selects Posted safe_drop rows by ShiftId. Reprinting a close slip recomputes detail from current rows but restores the stored expected, actual and difference headline.
specifications.impact: The closed shift close-slip component breakdown can reflect a later SafeDrop while its headline remains the original saved close values. This can reduce reconciliation clarity or attribute later custody to an earlier shift if that is not the intended policy.
implementation_blueprint: If prohibit: enforce shift-open state in a concurrency-safe transaction boundary shared with shift close.
If allow: represent later movement as an explicit post-close adjustment/revision and distinguish it from the immutable close snapshot in reprints.
required_regression_tests: Open BusinessDay and closed Shift: assert the owner-selected accepted/rejected outcome and posted movement ShiftId/BusinessDayId.
After close and any allowed later SafeDrop, reprint the slip and assert documented headline/component version semantics.
Race SafeDrop against CloseShift on the same shift using a disposable production-SQL-Server-provider test; assert a policy-valid serialized outcome.
If later posting is allowed, verify the audit/reprint distinguishes a later adjustment from cash present at original close.
acceptance_criteria: Owner decision is documented.
Stored close headline retains historical meaning.
Reprints either preserve close-time breakdown or clearly mark later adjustments.
Concurrent close/post outcomes obey the chosen policy.

specifications.title: Legacy WPF refund submit does not preserve the same idempotency key after an ambiguous outcome
specifications.root_cause: WPF SubmitRefundAsync creates a fresh RefundRequestId per invocation and WPF ApiClient does not expose transport ambiguity as OutcomeUnknown or retain the request for replay. WinUI keeps _pendingRefund and retries the same request ID during the current ViewModel lifetime.
specifications.impact: If WPF is supported/deployed, response loss after a successful partial refund can leave the operator without explicit unknown-outcome recovery; a subsequent submit generates a new key and may create a separate additional partial refund. Impact depends on deployment, transport outcome and operator action.
implementation_blueprint: If WPF is supported, route refund commands through explicit unknown-outcome state and retain/reconcile the same request ID before allowing a new submit. If WPF is retired, record that operational fact. Decide whether WinUI unresolved refund intent must survive restart; if so, persist a safe pending key or require authoritative refund lookup before another command. Preserve server amount and account guards.
required_regression_tests: Inject response loss after server commit in WPF; retry must reuse the key or require server reconciliation before a new command.
WinUI timeout/response loss then retry in same ViewModel must use the same ID and return one receipt.
Restart after unresolved WinUI outcome must follow owner-selected recovery policy.
A deliberate new partial refund with a distinct ID remains allowed when the order/account permit it.
Retain same-key replay and distinct-key cumulative cap integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: Owner documents whether WPF is supported or retired.
Supported clients cannot encourage a fresh financial command before prior outcome is resolved.
Same logical operation retains the idempotency key across retry; intentional new partial refunds remain distinct and auditable.

specifications.title: Held electronic preparation is not automatically released on confirmation
specifications.root_cause: Suppression is a one-time checkout decision without durable preparation-release state or confirmation outbox event.
specifications.impact: HoldPreparationUntilPaymentConfirmed suppresses initial kitchen routes. Confirmation posts money/status but does not enqueue held preparation. Auto-print documentation directs operator to Order Lookup.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Explicitly communicate manual release now; future approved implementation should persist held state and transactionally enqueue release with stable key on confirmation.
required_regression_tests: Add hold->confirm release exactly once, replay, mixed payment failure, cancellation-before-release and manual reprint tests.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Uncosted Waste Coercion to Zero in Loss Summary
specifications.root_cause: Null loss value on unpriced inventory item is coerced to zero.
specifications.impact: Understates financial spoilage figures in owner management reports.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Expose UnknownCostCount in LossSummaryDto to inform managers when loss values are incomplete.
required_regression_tests: Record waste on uncosted item; verify LossSummaryDto returns UnknownCostCount > 0.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory loss reporting explicitly distinguishes 0 EGP waste from unpriced uncosted waste.

specifications.title: CostingRules Yield Unit Conversion Uses Midpoint Banker's Rounding Causing Asymmetric Stock Deduction Truncation
specifications.root_cause: CostingRules.BaseQuantityMilliUnits applies default MidpointRounding.ToEven on single portion quantities before multiplying by order quantity, truncating fractional units.
specifications.impact: Asymmetric rounding truncation leads to cumulative inventory drift where physical stock and system stock diverge over time across high-volume recipe lines.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Compute total deducted base milliUnits across the entire ordered quantity using integer division with rounding: (line.QuantityMilliUnits * orderQuantity + ratio / 2) / ratio, or specify explicit MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero.
required_regression_tests: Calculate stock deduction for 3 units of an item with a yield ratio of 3 and 1000 milliUnits declared; verify total deducted milliUnits equals exactly 1000 rather than 999.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory stock deduction for yield-ratio recipe lines preserves exact aggregate integer milliUnits without rounding truncation.

specifications.title: Succeeded and print health collapse transport acceptance into physical completion
specifications.root_cause: Boolean transport contract has no acknowledgement level or spooler submission ID; job status has no accepted/unknown/confirmed distinction.
specifications.impact: Processor sets Succeeded after SendAsync returns. File write, TCP buffer acceptance and Windows RAW submission all satisfy this. Server overview derives last success from that flag; owner DTO comment describes physical output.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Use distinct Simulated, Submitted, SpoolerQueued, Failed, OutcomeUnknown and PhysicallyConfirmed observations. Never drain real pending jobs to file as production completion.
required_regression_tests: Existing success test verifies only fake transport Sent list. Add file-simulation status, paused spooler status under explicit authorization, and operator-confirmation tests.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Blocking spooler submission ignores cancellation and completion failures
specifications.root_cause: Timeout configuration applies to HTTP/TCP/serial write but not full native spooler lifecycle; unmanaged result handling is incomplete.
specifications.impact: Windows SendAsync calls blocking Send and discards cancellation. EndPagePrinter/EndDocPrinter results are ignored. Serial Open/Flush also block without cooperative cancellation.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Check finalization results, retain submission job ID, move blocking native submission to a controlled worker with bounded shutdown/uncertain outcome semantics.
required_regression_tests: Add injectable spooler API tests for failure and hang, short writes already checked in implementation; separate integration verification from physical output.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Agent never authenticates again after session loss
specifications.root_cause: No token-expiry or reauthentication recovery path; agent lifecycle assumes continuously sliding valid session.
specifications.impact: Login occurs once before poll loop. All subsequent 401 failures are logged and retried with same token indefinitely.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Add controlled reauthentication and explicit offline/authentication alarm without losing attempt journal or blindly resending uncertain jobs.
required_regression_tests: Add 401-then-authenticate recovery, deactivated-account terminal failure, and queued outcome reporting across reauth tests.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Saved printer width and receipt copy count do not control inspected print pipeline
specifications.root_cause: Persistence/UI configuration has no mapped consumer in render/dispatch implementation.
specifications.impact: Settings accepts PrinterWidth and NumberOfReceiptCopies, but auto-print creates one job per route and agent uses its own ImageWidthDots. Operators can save values that do not change output.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Define per-station paper capability and copy semantics; explicitly label unsupported settings until implemented. Copies must not multiply kitchen prep accidentally.
required_regression_tests: Add intended copy/width contract tests or disable unsupported setting UI.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Unguarded Read Access to Payroll Runs, Backups, Treasury, and Purchases
specifications.root_cause: Minimal API GET endpoints for payroll runs, backup metadata, treasury handovers, and supplier debts lack authorization policy filters or permission checks.
specifications.impact: Any authenticated low-privilege user can read sensitive business financial data including employee salaries, national IDs, treasury handovers, and supplier debt aging.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Apply RequirePermission(context, permission) filters to all sensitive read endpoints in Program.cs.
required_regression_tests: Issue GET /api/payroll-runs with standard cashier bearer token; verify 403 Forbidden.
Verify GET /api/backups requires backups_manage permission.
acceptance_criteria: All sensitive financial reporting and backup routes enforce explicit permission checks.

specifications.title: Approval Double-Spending Concurrency Hazard (CHALLENGED WITH COUNTEREVIDENCE)
specifications.root_cause: Earlier static analysis overlooked FalahDbContext's Fluent API configuration where Consumed is registered as an EF Core concurrency token.
specifications.impact: Mitigated in production by EF Core DbUpdateConcurrencyException; however, client receives an unhandled concurrency exception instead of a clean domain error message.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Retain concurrency token in FalahDbContext, and catch DbUpdateConcurrencyException in command handlers to translate to DomainException('اعتماد المدير مستخدم بالفعل').
required_regression_tests: Execute concurrent SaveChangesAsync marking the same ManagerApproval consumed; assert DbUpdateConcurrencyException is caught and translated to DomainException.
acceptance_criteria: Manager approval double-spending is strictly blocked by database-level concurrency token.

specifications.title: High PBKDF2 Computational Cost on PIN Uniqueness Validation
specifications.root_cause: Sequential synchronous evaluation of high-iteration PBKDF2 hashes across all active staff on server thread pool.
specifications.impact: Denial of service / thread pool starvation during user management operations.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Use deterministic HMAC blind indexing with a server pepper for O(1) uniqueness lookup, reserving PBKDF2 only for credential storage.
required_regression_tests: Benchmark AssertNotInUseAsync with 100 active user hashes; ensure execution completes under 50ms via blind indexing.
acceptance_criteria: PIN uniqueness validation scales in O(1) time without linear PBKDF2 recomputation.

specifications.title: User Deactivation Omits Explicit Session Token Revocation
specifications.root_cause: User deactivation modifies user entity status only, omitting explicit session revocation.
specifications.impact: Low immediate risk due to dynamic check; architectural risk of token survival across deactivation/reactivation cycles.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: In SetUserActiveHandler, mark all active sessions for the user as revoked (RevokedAtUtc = now).
required_regression_tests: Deactivate user; query UserSessions for userId; assert all active sessions have RevokedAtUtc populated.
acceptance_criteria: Deactivating an account explicitly revokes all issued session tokens.

specifications.title: Unselected expense and payment buttons combine literal white with dark-theme pale text
specifications.root_cause: Instance background bindings override correctly-themed SecondaryButtonStyle/PaymentMethodButtonStyle with WhiteBrush; text continues themed.
specifications.impact: Near-white labels on white surface, computed source-token contrast ~1.22:1, makes unselected choices hard to distinguish. User visual symptom consistent; reviewer has no actual screenshot and does not claim rendered pixel measurement.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Use coherent semantic card/neutral background with themed primary text for unselected state, direct ThemeResource/visual states for live updates; selected accent uses suitable contrast foreground.
required_regression_tests: Render all expense categories and all four payment methods selected/unselected in Light/Dark/System, unchanged and after live toggle; assert resolved text/background luminance and readable native screenshot.
Check disabled/hover/pressed states separately, preserving stored category values.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Imperative/converter brush results do not track live per-window theme reliably
specifications.root_cause: Converter returns concrete Brush object; unlike ThemeResource expression, no dependency informs it theme changed. Explicit dictionary lookup also does not traverse merged dictionaries.
specifications.impact: Selected/unselected/status colors can remain from previous or system theme, inconsistent with other surface/text resources. Exact WinUI fallback lookup result not runtime-proved.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Prefer theme-bound visual states/resources; explicitly observe ActualThemeChanged and traverse actual dictionary topology if imperative lookup retained.
required_regression_tests: Use real WinUI root RequestedTheme opposite system theme, compare ThemeResources.Get colors to descendant ThemeResource references.
Toggle repeatedly without changing Text/ExpenseCategory/PaymentMethod; compare same realized objects and brushes.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: A new pickup inherits previous order optional collection schedule
specifications.root_cause: Order reset named ResetDelivery also owns shared pickup customer fields but omits pickup-specific schedule.
specifications.impact: New customer order carries previous collection appointment or later fails past-time validation, unless operator notices and clears/changes type.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Reset optional schedule with resolved new-order lifecycle and explicit cart cancellation; keep historic order review separate.
required_regression_tests: Complete scheduled pickup using fake API, dismiss result, add next pickup; date/time and RequestedPickupAtUtc must be null until explicitly selected.
Repeat ClearCart/StartNewOrder and historic pending-order review to ensure intentional preserved live draft schedule is not erased.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Printer status UI exposes only four of six implemented routes
specifications.root_cause: Hardcoded status-route list lags shared print route vocabulary.
specifications.impact: No dedicated queue summary/filter for two routes; attention aggregate may still surface failed jobs. Not total invisibility claim.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Derive displayed route options from complete shared contract plus localized labels.
required_regression_tests: Provide overview with six routes and each pending/failed/stuck; assert all selectable and counts true.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Workspace shortcut guard omits most open operational modals
specifications.root_cause: Custom overlays do not centralize modal state and shortcut predicate only checks variant/payment/result.
specifications.impact: Potential underlying focus change, extra flyout or checkout sheet while another form open, risking confused data entry. Runtime keyboard reachability/focus path not executed.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Centralize IsAnyModalOpen plus accessible focus isolation and apply to all shortcuts.
required_regression_tests: Actual WinUI keyboard F2/F3/F12 + Tab/ShiftTab/Escape for every modal, assert no background focus/action and only one modal active.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Discarded definitively rejected CallCenter reprint survives in journal
specifications.root_cause: Safe discard memory path omits corresponding persistent store clear.
specifications.impact: Old rejected request reappears as ambiguous unresolved, can block fresh operation or queue an old reprint on retry when permissions/preconditions change. Does not prove duplicate sale.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Clear disk atomically when explicitly discarding known-rejected print; preserve unknown state separately.
required_regression_tests: Persist definite rejected print, clear through actual UI VM, reconstruct operator desk and assert no pending print/file.
Ambiguous failure must continue surviving same clear attempt.
specifications.acceptance_criteria: Invariant holds under retries and concurrent executions.

specifications.title: Legacy WPF change display parses EGP tender as integer piastres
specifications.root_cause: Display parses 100 as100 piastres or fails for100.00 while authoritative send converts to10000.
specifications.impact: Displayed change zero instead of10 EGP; server-recorded tender may still correct. Does not affect active WinUI CashInput change implementation.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: If WPF remains supported, use same tested CashInput units and notifications; otherwise prevent accidental deployment.
required_regression_tests: WPF ChangeDue test 90 EGP total with100 and100.00 tender both returns1000 piastres; Arabic/current-culture formats reviewed separately.

specifications.title: CallCenter lock/unlock retains old order-panel visual trees through cart subscription
specifications.root_cause: Long-lived cached VM Cart event holds every prior UserControl handler; subscriptions never removed on unload or DataContext replacement.
specifications.impact: Memory/native visual resource growth and repeated invisible callbacks over long shift; actual memory growth not measured.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Track subscribed VM, detach on change/unload, reattach once Loaded.
required_regression_tests: Native repeated lock/unlock, weak-reference old panel and force test GC; only current panel should remain.
DataContext A->B->A event subscription counts exactly1 and no callbacks on detached view.

specifications.title: Recipe yield conversion silently truncates fractional pieces-per-base-unit
specifications.root_cause: MilliUnits parser accepts fractional unit then conversion to integer floor without checking remainder.
specifications.impact: Stored recipe ratio differs from typed value and changes ingredient usage/cost calculation on future sales. No real recipe updated.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Validate integer divisibility before division or use dedicated localized positive-integer parser.

Whole numbers1,2and textual2.000 accepted exactly, enforce overflow bound.

specifications.title: Recipe ingredient picker truncates to60 choices without exposing its search input
specifications.root_cause: VM implemented bounded searchable choices but XAML exposes only ComboBox over current60 and no search binding to query full cached ingredients.
specifications.impact: Operator cannot directly find later ingredients through normal picker. Recipe may remain incomplete or user may choose wrong similar item; no actual recipe mutation tested.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Bind explicit ingredient search to IngredientSearchText or provide searchable full-list picker; disclose bounds only as presentation optimization.
required_regression_tests: Load61+ active ingredients with nonechosen; entering target61 search should exposeit without adding unrelated ingredients.
Exclude chosenIDs while searching fullcached inventory; clearing search should preserve selected choice and exact recipe lines.

specifications.title: EmployeesViewModel Sequentially Executes N+1 API Calls for Balances and Exits Early on First Failure Leaving Employee List Empty
specifications.root_cause: Sequential N+1 API balance calls in UI loading routine coupled with catastrophic early exit on single failure prior to applying display filter.
specifications.impact: A single network hiccup or unmapped employee ledger record results in the entire employee list disappearing from the UI, blocking shift attendance and payroll operations.
specifications.implementation_blueprint: Introduce a bulk employee balance endpoint on the server, or fetch balances concurrently with Task.WhenAll and gracefully degrade individual failed balances while still displaying successfully loaded employees.
required_regression_tests: Simulate employee balance API failure for 1 out of 10 employees; assert EmployeesViewModel displays remaining 9 employees and shows non-blocking warning rather than an empty list.
acceptance_criteria: EmployeesViewModel displays all successfully loaded employees even if an individual employee balance lookup fails, and eliminates sequential N+1 network requests.
